original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compare-cosk0}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a morphism
of presheaves of sets. Denote $K$ the simplicial
object of $\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$ whose $n$th
term is the $(n + 1)$st fibre product of $\mathcal{F}$
over $\mathcal{G}$, see
Simplicial, Example \ref{simplicial-example-fibre-products-simplicial-object}.
Then, if $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is surjective after
sheafification, we have
$$
H_i(K) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
0 & \text{if} & i > 0\\
\mathbf{Z}_\mathcal{G}^\# & \text{if} & i = 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
The isomorphism in degree $0$ is given by the
morphism $H_0(K) \to \mathbf{Z}_\mathcal{G}^\#$
coming from the map $(\mathbf{Z}_K^\#)_0 =
\mathbf{Z}_\mathcal{F}^\# \to \mathbf{Z}_\mathcal{G}^\#$.

review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L662 and Stage A logical fields: For matching n-coskeletal simplicial presheaves, isomorphism in levels below n and a sheafified epi in level n induces a quasi-isomorphism of sheafified free-abelian chain complexes. All four source hypotheses and all homology degrees are preserved.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $f : L \to K$ be a morphism of
simplicial objects of $\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $i < n$ the morphism $L_i \to K_i$ is an isomorphism.
\item The morphism $L_n \to K_n$ is surjective after sheafification.
\item The canonical map $L \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n L$ is an isomorphism.
\item The canonical map $K \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n K$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H_i(f) : H_i(L) \to H_i(K)$ is an isomorphism.
Here $H_i(-)$ denotes homology of the complex of free-abelian sheaves on the simplicial presheaf, as defined in hypercovering.tex L572–586.

review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L717 and Stage A logical fields: The augmented simplicial presheaf satisfying level-zero, level-one and all higher sheafified matching surjections is a hypercover in the sense of local homology descent, so H_i(K)=0 for positive i and H_0(K)=Z_G^#. Each indexed condition is retained.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $K$ be a simplicial presheaf.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf.
Let $K \to \mathcal{G}$ be an augmentation of $K$
towards $\mathcal{G}$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism of presheaves $K_0 \to \mathcal{G}$ becomes
a surjection after sheafification.
\item The morphism
$$
(d^1_0, d^1_1) :
K_1
\longrightarrow
K_0 \times_\mathcal{G} K_0
$$
becomes a surjection after sheafification.
\item For every $n \geq 1$ the morphism
$$
K_{n + 1} \longrightarrow (\text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n K)_{n + 1}
$$
turns into a surjection after sheafification.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H_i(K) = 0$ for $i > 0$ and
$H_0(K) = \mathbf{Z}_\mathcal{G}^\#$.
Here $H_i(-)$ denotes homology of the complex of free-abelian sheaves on the simplicial presheaf, as defined in hypercovering.tex L572–586.

review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L783 and Stage A logical fields: The sheafified free-abelian complex associated with an object hypercover F(K) resolves Z_X^#: local matching surjectivity kills positive homology and degree-zero is the representable free sheaf. The three definitions are supplied, not made premises.
statement:
For an indexed family $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ in a category $\mathcal C$, write $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C)$ for the category of semi-representable families, and let $F$ be the functor sending such a family to the presheaf $\coprod_{i\in I}h_{U_i}$ (hypercovering.tex L110–155).
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
The homology of the simplicial presheaf $F(K)$ is
$0$ in degrees $> 0$ and equal to $\mathbf{Z}_X^\#$
in degree $0$.
A hypercovering of an object $X$ in a site $\mathcal C$ with fibre products means a simplicial object $K$ of $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C,X)$ whose level-zero family covers $X$ and for each $n\ge0$ whose morphism $K_{n+1}\to (\mathrm{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK)_{n+1}$ is a covering (hypercovering.tex L345–359).
Here $H_i(-)$ denotes homology of the complex of free-abelian sheaves on the simplicial presheaf, as defined in hypercovering.tex L572–586.
